headline_cluster.headline: פוטין רוצה לחיות לנצח? נחשף כמה כסף רוסיה משקיעה בזה

primary_source_search_status: found_via_search_snippets: figure traces to The Wall Street Journal (~late May 2026; WSJ X post 'Vladimir Putin is on a $26 billion quest for immortality'): ~$26B / ~2 trillion rubles through 2030 for the national project 'New Health Preservation Technologies' (Новые технологии сбережения здоровья). Hebrew coverage (Calcalist, Israel Hayom) repeats $26B (~84B NIS). Russian-language reporting gives a conflicting, ~10x smaller total (~210B rubles: ~60B federal + ~150B extrabudgetary, ≈$2.6B); a separate Moscow Times piece (2026-07-26) reports Russian Science Foundation aging grants (43 projects 2021-25; min. 172M rubles). WSJ, Moscow Times, pnp.ru, gxpnews, wionews, tbsnews, turkiyetoday all EGRESS_BLOCKED for WebFetch; figures from consistent search snippets only. Searched EN/HE/RU.

claims.claim: נחשף כמה כסף רוסיה משקיעה ב'לחיות לנצח' (הכותרת לא נוקבת בסכום; לפי הסיקור העברי המקביל ככל הנראה ~26 מיליארד דולר)
claims.verified_figure: WSJ: ~$26B (~2 trillion rubles) to 2030 for the entire national project 'New Health Preservation Technologies' — five federal projects (medical science management; drugs/devices/platforms; biomedical & cognitive tech; regenerative/preventive/healthy-longevity; healthcare industry/import substitution). Longevity/anti-aging is one strand, not the whole budget. Russian-language reporting gives ~210B rubles (≈$2.6B) total; aging-specific RSF grants are in the millions of dollars.
claims.article_figure_per_search_snippet: Walla body unreachable; the exact Walla figure is not confirmed. Hebrew coverage of the same story (Calcalist, Israel Hayom) says $26B (~84B NIS), 'according to expert estimates', for Putin's anti-aging project.
claims.note: The $26B figure exists in reputable reporting (WSJ), but it is the budget of a broad health-tech national project. The 'live forever' framing assigns all of it to anti-aging, which inflates the scope. The figure is also disputed: Russian-language parliamentary reporting gives a total about 10x smaller (~210B rubles), and the gap was not resolved. Putin's personal motives are framing and out of scope. Low confidence: the Walla body was not read, so the verdict rests on attributing the widely circulated $26B figure to this headline.
